title: Streaming object mappers for typed response schemas + retry-safe hydration
creator: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:
We need a robust, ergonomic way for Python SDK users to consume streaming responses as typed model instances while preserving correctness across retries, partial streams, and schema evolution. Current SDK helpers either force the user to buffer full responses before parsing (bad for latency) or provide ad-hoc chunk parsers that don't guarantee model invariants or safe retries.

Goals:
- Provide a streaming-to-object mapper that incrementally builds typed models (dataclass or pydantic) as tokens/chunks arrive.
- Ensure retry safety: when a request is retried, previously emitted objects should not violate at-least-once/at-most-once guarantees depending on the configured policy.
- Support schema evolution: allow optional/ignored fields, and provide clear migration hooks when required fields appear/disappear.
- Offer simple ergonomic APIs for common use-cases (line-delimited JSON events, chunked JSON fields, partial text + structured parts).
- Provide example cookbooks and tests demonstrating backpressure handling, cancellation, and graceful degradation to raw stream fallback.

Proposal / Design:
1) Public API: StreamMapper[T] + stream_to_objects() helper
   - StreamMapper is a thin abstraction that takes a typed target class (dataclass or pydantic.BaseModel) and a small config object (delimiter, json_path, chunk_assembler, merge_policy).
   - stream_to_objects(client.stream(...), mapper) returns an async iterator AsyncIterator[T] that yields fully hydrated objects as soon as required fields are present.
   - Synchronous wrapper: stream_to_objects_sync(...) for users not on asyncio (uses thread executor but backpressure-friendly).

2) Incremental hydration semantics:
   - The mapper uses a pluggable assembler that accumulates partial JSON/text across event chunks. Default assembler supports:
     a) newline-delimited JSON (ndjson)
     b) JSON objects split across chunks (reassembly with bracket matching)
     c) structured text with a final JSON payload (prefix text then JSON chunk)
   - Hydration triggers when assembler detects a complete JSON object or when a user-provided predicate is satisfied (eg. presence of required field).
   - For pydantic targets: use model.parse_obj for final validation; for dataclasses: cast + manual validation helpers. Provide an adapter layer to translate pydantic validation errors into uniform SDK exceptions (StructuredOutputError).

3) Retry-safety model:
   - Add a per-request header "X-Redwood-Stream-Id" returned by the server and echoed on retries. The mapper uses that plus an idempotency token from client to deduplicate objects across retry boundaries when client config 'dedupe_on_retry' is true.
   - When dedupe_on_retry=false (default), we provide a clear warning in docs: streaming endpoints may produce duplicates during network retries.
   - Provide a convenience utility DedupeWindow that keeps a configurable sliding window of recently seen object hashes to avoid duplicates in common cases (memory-bounded).

4) Backpressure and cancellation:
   - Async iterator respects consumer speed by pausing underlying network read when internal buffer reach high-water mark and resumes when drained.
   - Expose mapper.cancel(reason) to early-cancel parsing and optionally request server-side abort if supported (via a cancel token).

5) Schema evolution and migrations:
   - Mapper supports field aliases and a schema_compatibility flag: "lenient" (ignore extra fields, treat missing fields as None when optional) or "strict" (raise StructuredOutputError on mismatch).
   - Add a migration hook that can be registered per StreamMapper to transform incoming dicts before validation (useful when the server changed field names).

6) Examples and cookbooks:
   - Line-delimited events to pydantic models (real-time metrics ingestion).
   - Long-running chat stream that yields Message dataclasses as soon as content_id and text are available, while streaming tokens still arrive for content.
   - Retry-safe ingestion example showing idempotency tokens and DedupeWindow.

Acceptance criteria:
- API implemented in python-sdk/runtime and shipped behind feature flag: python-sdk.typed_streaming_beta.
- Unit tests covering: ndjson reassembly, chunked-object reassembly, assembler predicate triggers, pydantic/dataclass hydration, duplicate suppression, backpressure behavior (high-water/low-water simulation), cancel paths, and schema_compatibility modes.
- Integration test with a harness server that can inject chunk boundaries and connection resets to validate retry/dedup behavior.
- Documentation: a short guide in docs/sdk/python/streaming-objects.md and three cookbooks in examples/python/streaming_cookbooks/; PRs linked below.
- No user-facing breaking changes to existing sync streaming APIs; this is additive.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Dedup on retry requires server cooperation (stream id) for robust semantics; we can fall back to client-only dedupe but might get false positives/negatives. Decision: implement client-only DedupeWindow now and product follow-up to add stream ids + server dedupe.
- Pydantic v2 adoption: should the mapper require pydantic v2 or support v1? We'll support both via a thin adapter layer but default tests run on pydantic>=2 in CI.
- Memory vs correctness: DedupeWindow size is a knob; default 5000 objects. Document costs.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1: implement assembler primitives + unit tests (ndjson, bracket matching). (Owner: Liam)
- Week 2: implement StreamMapper and pydantic/dataclass adapters + validation error mapping. (Owner: Liam)
- Week 3: implement dedupe utilities, backpressure integration, cancellation token, and sync wrapper. (Owner: Samir Patel)
- Week 4: integration harness, docs, cookbooks, and internal SDK rollout behind feature flag. (Owner: Maya Chen)

Progress updates:
- 2026-02-15 (Liam O'Connor): Started assembler unit tests; ndjson passes. Bracket-matching edge case for nested arrays failing intermittently when objects contain stringified JSON; added tests to reproduce.
- 2026-02-20 (Maya Chen): Added pydantic adapter prototype. Confirmed pydantic v1/v2 adapter approach works locally. Open task: unify error types in SDK exceptions.
- 2026-02-28 (Samir Patel): Implemented DedupeWindow with LRU-backed ring buffer; basic tests pass. Need to exercise at-scale memory usage in integration harness.
- 2026-03-05 (Liam O'Connor): Hooked backpressure into internal httpx stream reader; manual test with slow consumer shows pause/resume working. Edge-case: when consumer dies without cancel, connection stays open — added cancel() to iterator but need server-side abort integration.

PRs for review:
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/842 (assembler + iterator)
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/849 (pydantic/dataclass adapters)
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/863 (dedupe + backpressure)

Validation / testing checklist (to close ticket):
- [ ] Unit tests: assembler, adapter, dedupe, cancel, backpressure
- [ ] Integration test: chunked resets + retry dedupe check
- [ ] Docs: streaming-objects.md guide + 3 cookbooks added
- [ ] API review: public API reviewed by SDK owners and typed-output SIG
- [ ] Security review: confirm no PII leakage in dedupe window and logs

Rollout plan:
- Start behind feature flag python-sdk.typed_streaming_beta for one week with internal dogfooding customers.
- Collect telemetry: duplicate rate, memory usage, consumer cancellation frequency, parser errors.
- After stabilization (2 weeks), flip flag and ship in minor release python-sdk-2026.03.

Next steps (short term):
- Finish PR #842 tests (bracket matching edge cases) — Liam — 2d
- Add migration hook example to docs — Maya — 3d
- Add integration harness scenario where server returns stream id header and verify dedupe works end-to-end — Samir — 5d

Comments:
- 2026-03-09 (PM review - Priya Desai): Please call out expected consumer semantics clearly in docs (exactly-once not guaranteed unless server dedupe supported). Good to add a small checklist for migration for teams that previously used naive chunk parsers.
- 2026-03-10 (Design review - Elena Ortiz): Strong +1 on migration hook. Recommend adding warning-level logs when parse errors occur and option to emit raw_event hooks to Sentry for auditing.
